chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and gave her a dowry, then sent to her sheep and slaves, and she bore children by him, so he divorced her before entering into her.

He said: 'If he had sent to her what he sent, and she had borne children by him, then half of the dowry is his and half of the children are his; and if she had borne children by him, then he has nothing from the children.'
Of the wealth or from their two shares. He said: 'From all the wealth, for it is in the position of a debt.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial and custodial rights of a husband who divorces his wife before consummation after giving her a dowry and gifts?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the division of dowry and offspring in a pre-consummation divorce, establishing that the man's entitlement to half the wealth and children is contingent upon the actual delivery of the gifted assets. The Imam further elucidates that this financial claim is treated as a debt against the total estate, a nuance that distinguishes it from simple proportional division. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the status of 'gifts' (*hibah*) within the marital contract and their impact on the rights of the wife and children when the marriage is dissolved before intimacy.
